steps.title: Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have your back and neck felt since you finished decompression care?

I usually hear one of three things. Still feeling great, starting to come back, or pretty much back to before.

Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Doing Great
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes care with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Starting to Come Back
steps.content:
Thanks for telling me, {{contact_first_name}}. That can happen as pressure builds again over time.

Your notes say you had good relief when you finished. What do you think brought it back?

(Let them answer. Be kind. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Fully Back
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. That's frustrating.

Your notes say you had good relief when you finished. What do you think brought it back?

(Let them answer. Be kind. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask you a few quick questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{complaint_reference}} is starting to come back. We'll come back to that.

First, can I ask a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every issue they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Have you had any neck pain?

Have you had any back pain?

Are you having trouble sitting?

Does any pain travel down a leg or arm?

Do you have morning stiffness?

Are you having trouble bending or lifting?

Have you had any flare-ups?

Are there activities you've given up because of it?

Of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Questions: Symptoms Returning
steps.content:
(Include what they mentioned earlier as you write down each issue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Have you had any neck pain?

Have you had any back pain?

Are you having trouble sitting?

Does any pain travel down a leg or arm?

Do you have morning stiffness?

Are you having trouble bending or lifting?

Have you had any flare-ups?

Are there activities you've given up because of it?

Between these and what returned, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask three quick questions about {{main_concern}}.

(Ask each question in order. Let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we may be able to help with.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can look at {{main_concern}} and your decompression progress. If decompression can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything.

Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why They Stopped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad you're still doing well.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in for check-ins?

(Let them answer. Do not argue with it.)

Decompression can ease pressure, but everyday strain can build again. Regular checks help us catch changes early.

(Tap the reason they shared.)

steps.title: Objection: “It came back after I stopped”
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me, {{contact_first_name}}. That's one of the most common reasons people call us back.

How long after your last session did you notice it?

(Let them answer.)

When it comes back that soon, it usually means the pressure was down but the area hadn't fully settled. Care stopped a little early, or life loaded it up faster than expected. Either way, you're not back at square one. You already did the hard part once.

We'd rather have {{provider_name}} check it now than let it build back up. You'll hear where things stand and what it would take.

Can we get you in for a look?

steps.title: Objection: “I thought it was fixed for good”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Most people finish decompression expecting the relief to hold.

Can I ask what's changed since you finished, like more sitting, driving, or lifting?

(Let them answer.)

Your notes say you were moving better when you finished. So the care did its job. What didn't change is the load on that spot. Long days sitting or lifting put the pressure right back. That's why it crept back, and it doesn't mean the care failed.

Let's have {{provider_name}} check what changed. If it's a short tune-up, you'll know. If it's something new, you'll know that too.

Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Objection: Injections or Surgery
steps.content:
Okay. That tells me it's gotten bad enough that you want it handled.

Has a doctor recommended that, or is it something you're looking into yourself?

(Let them answer. Do not talk down injections or surgery.)

Both of those are real options, and sometimes they're the right call. They're also hard to undo once you've done them. Decompression is one of the things people try before going that route. A visit with {{provider_name}} doesn't rule anything out. It gives you a second look at {{main_concern}} before you commit to something permanent.

If decompression isn't the answer here, we'll say so. Either way you'll walk into that decision knowing more than you do today.

Does it make sense to get that second look first?

steps.title: If They Say: “I was feeling fine”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When you feel good, a check-in stops feeling urgent.

Pressure can build before you notice a change. A check-in helps us see how your back is holding up.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule while you're feeling good. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m managing on my own”
steps.content:
Good for you, {{contact_first_name}}. That takes some discipline.

What have you been doing for it?

(Let them answer. Give them credit for it.)

Stretching and home care can keep you moving, and that matters. What they can't do is take the pressure off the way decompression does. Managing something and fixing it are two different things.

A check with {{provider_name}} tells you which one you're dealing with. If what you're doing is enough, we'll tell you to keep going. If it isn't, you'll find out now instead of a year from now.

Would it help to know for sure?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. You're not committing to more decompression care today.

The first step is one visit so we can check how things are holding.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule for a check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and a check-in gets pushed down the list.

We can find a time that works around your schedule. Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule at an easy time. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back if it hurts”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Pressure can build before pain gets your attention.

A check-in lets us look before it becomes harder to manage. Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule for a check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Moved or Tried Another Office
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change.

If you're still nearby, we'd be glad to see you. Your decompression history is already in your file.

Would coming back here be an option?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Transition: Symptoms Fully Back
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{complaint_reference}} is pretty much back. We'll come back to that.

First, can I ask a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: Symptoms Fully Back
steps.content:
(Include the symptoms already back as you write down each issue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Have you had any neck pain?

Have you had any back pain?

Are you having trouble sitting?

Does any pain travel down a leg or arm?

Do you have morning stiffness?

Are you having trouble bending or lifting?

Have you had any flare-ups?

Are there activities you've given up because of it?

Including what came back, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like physical therapy, massage, or another office?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all help, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what's going on with {{main_concern}} right now. {{provider_name}} already has your history and knows how you responded last time, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it more the cost of the visit itself, or not knowing what insurance will cover?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Insurance changes every year, so a lot of people aren't sure what they have now. Our front desk can check your coverage before you come in, so there are no surprises. And this first visit is one appointment, not another round of sessions. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “It’s the time or number of visits”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first visit, or the worry about coming in several times a week like before?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that's a handful of visits to settle it down. Sometimes it's more, and you'll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is signing you up for a full series on the phone.

We have early and late openings. Since you've been here before, the first visit is usually under 30 minutes.

Could you find half an hour for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that the pressure is back and you don't know why. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} has been building for a while now. It's had time to sort itself out on its own, and it hasn't. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send information”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you whether {{main_concern}} is the same spot acting up or something new. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at you, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
